scenes.text: Imagine you commit a serious crime deep inside a remote section of Yellowstone National Park, but an unbelievable constitutional loophole prevents the police from ever arresting you.
This fifty-square-mile strip of wilderness is widely known as the Zone of Death, because it sits in Idaho but remains under Wyoming's federal court jurisdiction.

Since the United States Constitution strictly demands a jury be chosen only from the state and district where the crime occurred, and absolutely zero people live in this specific area, forming a legal jury is physically impossible.

Even though Congress has known about this terrifying lawless glitch for decades, they have never fixed it, so would you ever dare to spend a night camping in this dangerous zone? Let me know in the comments below.
